title: Conditional first-passage Poisson bridge for boundary response
question: If the Q3 response admits a nonnegative factorial first-passage expansion, does graph degree and a spatial weight yield a volume-uniform boundary decay bound?

hypothesis.response_expansion: R_x(t) <= sum_{n>=0} (eta*t)^n/n! sum_{paths gamma ending at x, length n} R_{gamma(0)}(0)
hypothesis.path_count: At most z^n paths of length n leave any starting site
hypothesis.support: R_y(0)=0 outside a finite source set X
hypothesis.distance: Every path from X to x has length at least d(x,X)
hypothesis.status: OPEN for the exact Q3 onsite-plus-bond dynamics

bridge.interpretation: This is a conditional first-passage bridge, not an actual Q3 locality theorem

scope.closed: Exact factorial path-sum to weighted boundary-decay arithmetic under the declared hypothesis
scope.open: Actual Q3 first-passage expansion, onsite recurrence, projected Duhamel locality, exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha, KMS, ground/gap, continuum and Pre-A
scope.not_claimed: Q3 dynamics, thermodynamic locality, C6 closure, Sector A closure or TECT production ownership

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only the rational rate, weight and finite-distance fixture arithmetic; it does not encode the infinite path expansion

no_overclaim: The bridge is conditional on an unproved Q3 factorial path expansion and path-count bound. It supplies a precise target for the open boundary gate but does not prove Q3 dynamics, common alpha, KMS, a mass gap, Pre-A, Sector A or the TECT production map.
